subtitle: How One Poet’s Song Bound Love, Raga and Devotion Across Ages

panels.shot: low-angle three-quarter wide of a poet under a lamplit verandah, palm-leaf manuscript in hand, temple silhouettes and a distant sea behind him
panels.action: Jayadeva stands in loose ascetic-poet garb beneath a darkening sky, holding a palm-leaf manuscript as waves glimmer beyond and faint temple towers rise along the horizon.

dialogue.text: In Lakshmanasena’s age, Jayadeva sang Radha’s return—one poem that slipped court walls, crossed temples and tongues, and still refuses to be claimed by any single land.

i18n.hi: लक्ष्मणसेन के समय में जयदेव ने गाई राधा की लौट – एक कविता जो दरबार की दीवारों से फिसलकर मंदिरों और ज़ुबानों को पार कर गई, जिसे आज तक कोई एक धरती अपना नहीं कह पाती।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high angle over a palm-leaf manuscript laid on the floor, script visible but unreadable, oil lamp casting a warm pool of light
panels.action: Jayadeva sits cross-legged beside an oil lamp, bent over a fresh palm-leaf, the etched lines of Sanskrit script catching the flicker of the flame.

dialogue.text: We begin not on a battlefield, but on a leaf of palm. Twelve chapters, twenty-four songs, each set to raga and tala—Jayadeva’s Gita Govinda is born as music written into verse.

i18n.hi: युद्धभूमि नहीं, हम शुरू करते हैं ताड़पत्र से। बारह अध्याय, चौबीस गीत, हर एक राग और ताल में ढला – जयदेव का गीतगोविंद जन्मता है, कविता में लिखा संगीत बनकर।

panels.shot: wide aerial over the Ganga delta, rivers braiding through fields, with distant city walls suggesting Nabadwip
panels.action: The camera glides over braided rivers and green fields towards a walled town with spires and tiled roofs rising above the misty floodplains.

dialogue.text: In the late twelfth century, Bengal’s rivers carried more than grain. Under king Lakshmanasena of the Sena line, courts in places like Nabadwip drew poets and pundits from across the east.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं शताब्दी के उत्तरार्ध में, बंगाल की नदियाँ सिर्फ़ अन्न नहीं ढोतीं। सेना वंश के राजा लक्ष्मणसेन के अधीन नवद्वीप जैसे दरबारों में पूरब भर के कवि और पंडित उमड़ पड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: medium interior of a court hall, pillars framing seated scholars as Jayadeva stands at one side, slightly apart
panels.action: In a high-pillared hall, courtiers sit in rows while Jayadeva, simple in dress, stands quietly near a column, listening as another court poet recites before the king.

dialogue.text: Later tradition places Jayadeva among Lakshmanasena’s poets—names like Dhoyi and Umapati Dhara echo beside his. In these halls, polished Sanskrit praise met the rustle of royal power.

i18n.hi: बाद की परंपरा जयदेव को लक्ष्मणसेन के राजकवि कहलवाती है – धोई, उमापति धरा जैसे नाम उसके साथ गूँजते हैं। इन्हीं सभाओं में चमकदार संस्कृत स्तुति, राजसत्ता की सरसराहट से टकराती है।

panels.shot: close-up on Jayadeva’s face in three-quarter profile, eyes distant, court scene blurred behind him
panels.action: Jayadeva’s face fills the frame, his gaze turned away from the throne, the debate of scholars behind him dissolving into a soft blur.

dialogue.text: But Jayadeva’s mind wandered beyond courtly panegyrics. His verse reached for Radha and Krishna, for longing and reunion, sung as much as spoken.

i18n.hi: पर जयदेव का मन दरबारी प्रशंसा से आगे भटकता है। उसकी कविता राधा–कृष्ण की, विरह और मिलन की, सुनाई ही नहीं, गाई भी जाती है।

panels.shot: medium shot in a modest home courtyard, Jayadeva chanting while a small group listens, a musician with cymbals beside him
panels.action: In a sunlit courtyard, Jayadeva stands bare-foot, eyes closed, as he chants; a simple musician marks time with small cymbals while villagers listen at the doorway.

dialogue.text: The Gita Govinda is not a dry treatise. Each ashtapadi is marked with raga and tala, instructions that tie its words to melody, its theology to the sway of a singing body.

i18n.hi: गीतगोविंद सूखी शास्त्र–पुस्तक नहीं। हर अष्टपदी पर राग–ताल के चिन्ह, जो शब्दों को धुन से, दर्शन को गाते शरीर की लय से बाँध देते हैं।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind Jayadeva as he inscribes raga and tala names on the palm leaf
panels.action: From behind Jayadeva’s shoulder, his hand is seen scratching delicate script into the palm-leaf, the names of ragas and talas etched alongside the verses.

dialogue.text: Barbara Stoler Miller and later editors point to these notations—clear signs that the poem was designed for performance, its structure a score as well as scripture.

i18n.hi: बारबरा स्टोलर मिलर और बाद के संपादक इन्हीं निशानों की ओर इशारा करते हैं – साफ़ संकेत कि यह काव्य गाए जाने के लिए रचा गया, इसकी बनावट रचना भी है, शास्त्र भी।

panels.shot: wide shot of a temple street in eastern India, with a shrine in the background and Jayadeva walking in the foreground, a travel staff in hand
panels.action: On a bustling temple street lined with carved facades, Jayadeva walks with a staff and bundle, glancing up at a distant shrine tower that rises above the town.

dialogue.text: Later Odisha traditions claim him as their own, Bengal ones do the same. The record stays silent; inscription and text do not settle one birthplace, even as both regions weave him into their memory.

i18n.hi: बाद की ओड़िया परंपरा उसे अपना बताती है, बंगाल भी। शिलालेख चुप हैं, पांडुलिपियाँ भी जन्मस्थान नहीं ठहरातीं, जबकि दोनों प्रदेश उसे अपनी स्मृति में पिरोते रहते हैं।

panels.shot: majestic wide shot of the Jagannatha temple complex from a distance, with Jayadeva tiny in the foreground
panels.action: The towering spire of the Jagannatha temple dominates the skyline as Jayadeva, a small figure near the base, looks up toward the stone colossus in awed stillness.

dialogue.text: In Puri’s Jagannatha tradition, the Gita Govinda becomes woven into temple ritual. Priests, dancers, singers—each takes Jayadeva’s verses into the daily service of the deity.

i18n.hi: पुरी की जगन्नाथ परंपरा में गीतगोविंद मंदिर की रीत में घुल जाता है। पुजारी, नर्तक, गायक – सब जयदेव के पदों को देव–सेवा की रोज़मर्रा में उतारते हैं।

panels.shot: interior wide of a temple mandapa, dancers mid-pose before the deity, Jayadeva seated to one side, reciting
panels.action: Inside a stone mandapa lit by lamps, dancers hold a graceful pose before the sanctum while Jayadeva, seated at the side, recites with one hand raised in gentle emphasis.

dialogue.text: The poem gives them a script of devotion. Radha’s jealousy, Krishna’s pleading, the final embrace—Gita Govinda turns theology into drama, allowing worship to be danced and sung.

i18n.hi: काव्य उन्हें भक्ति की पटकथा देता है। राधा की जलेसी, कृष्ण की मनुहार, आख़िरी आलिंगन – गीतगोविंद दर्शन को नाटक में बदल देता है, ताकि पूजा नाचकर और गाकर हो सके।

panels.shot: tight close-up of Jayadeva’s lips and hand as he recites a tender verse, background fading into soft bokeh
panels.action: Jayadeva’s lips are caught mid-verse, his fingers lightly beating rhythm on his knee, the background dissolving into soft circles of light.

i18n.hi: "राधे, लौट आओ – हमारा अर्घ्य बने ये प्रेम।"

panels.shot: montage-style wide panel divided subtly into three scenes of different landscapes, each with singers holding manuscripts
panels.action: Three vignettes share the frame: a village in eastern India, a distant northern shrine, and another in the west, in each a singer holds a palm manuscript while others sit listening.

dialogue.text: From Bengal to Odisha and beyond, the poem travels with singers and scribes. Copies multiply, variants appear, but the core arc of separation and return remains the same.

i18n.hi: बंगाल से ओड़िशा और आगे, यह काव्य गायकों और लिपिकारों के साथ चलता है। प्रतियाँ फैलती हैं, रूप बदलते हैं, पर विरह और पुनर्मिलन की धुरी वही रहती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Sikh granthi in a later-century setting, seated before the Guru Granth Sahib, pointing to a hymn
panels.action: Centuries later, a Sikh granthi sits before the open Guru Granth Sahib, finger resting on a hymn as devotees sit cross-legged nearby in quiet attention.

dialogue.text: Evidence of its afterlife lies in an unexpected place. The Guru Granth Sahib preserves hymns attributed to Jayadeva in Raag Gujri—fragments of his voice carried into a different devotional world.

i18n.hi: उसकी अगली ज़िंदगी का सबूत एक अनपेक्षित जगह में है। गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में राग गुजरी पर जयदेव के नाम से भजन दर्ज हैं – उसकी आवाज़ के टुकड़े एक और भक्ति–जगत में पहुँचते हुए।

panels.shot: close-up on the script of the Guru Granth Sahib page, the name 'Jaidev' indicated by the granthi’s finger, faces of listeners soft in the background
panels.action: The camera tightens on the script as the granthi’s finger rests near the line naming ‘Jaidev’, the blurred faces of listeners forming a halo behind the text.

dialogue.text: Here Jayadeva is no longer a court poet, nor a regional saint; he is one voice among many, his verses folded into a canon that crosses yet another set of boundaries.

i18n.hi: यहाँ जयदेव न दरबारी कवि है, न किसी एक प्रदेश का संत; वह कई स्वरों में एक स्वर है, जिसकी पंक्तियाँ ऐसे ग्रंथ में घुलती हैं जो नई सीमाएँ भी पार करता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Jayadeva older, seated alone at dusk, rolling up a palm-leaf manuscript, river glinting behind
panels.action: An older Jayadeva sits at the riverbank at dusk, gently rolling up a palm manuscript as birds wheel over the darkening water.

dialogue.text: The historical record gives no clear ending for him—no solid tomb, no definite village. What survives instead is the work itself, endlessly copied, sung, re-staged in new voices.

i18n.hi: इतिहास उसे साफ़ अंत नहीं देता – न पक्की मज़ार, न पक्का गाँव। जो बचा है, वह सिर्फ़ रचना है, बार–बार नकल होती, गाई जाती, नई आवाज़ों में फिर से खेले जाने के लिए।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of dancers in a modern classical dance performance, with a translucent superimposed image of Jayadeva observing from the side
panels.action: A contemporary stage shows classical dancers poised mid-step, while a faint, translucent image of Jayadeva stands at the wings, watching with a calm, unreadable expression.

dialogue.text: Modern Odissi and other dance forms still return to Gita Govinda. Choreographers mine its ashtapadis, treating Jayadeva as a living collaborator across eight centuries.

i18n.hi: आज का ओडिसी और दूसरी नृत्य–शैलियाँ बार–बार गीतगोविंद की ओर लौटती हैं। नृत्य–निर्देशक उसकी अष्टपदियों को टटोलते हैं, मानो आठ सौ साल बाद भी जयदेव उनका ज़िंदा सह–रचनाकार हो।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Jayadeva’s eyes, reflecting a flickering lamp as if seeing both temple and court
panels.action: Jayadeva’s eyes fill the frame, tiny reflections of a temple lamp and a court hall flickering together in his gaze.

dialogue.text: Legends grow around him, as they do around all beloved poets. Yet scholars trace what they can: the structure of the poem, its musical cues, its place in the wider Sanskrit and bhakti traditions.

i18n.hi: किंवदंतियाँ उसके चारों ओर उगती हैं, जैसे हर प्रिय कवि के साथ होता है। फिर भी विद्वान जो पकड़ सकते हैं, पकड़ते हैं – काव्य की बनावट, उसके संगीत–संकेत, संस्कृत और भक्ति की बड़ी परंपरा में उसकी जगह।

panels.shot: wide shot of a present-day library or archive reading room, a scholar studying a palm-leaf manuscript while a faded mural of Radha-Krishna adorns the wall; Jayadeva’s figure imagined faintly beside
panels.action: In a bright reading room, a modern scholar leans over a palm-leaf manuscript under glass, while on the wall behind, a faded Radha-Krishna mural watches; a faint, imagined Jayadeva stands near the mural, almost blending into it.

dialogue.text: Editors like Lee Siegel and others re-examine manuscripts, variants, commentaries. They treat Gita Govinda as both art and historical artifact, mapping how one work moved through courts, temples and printed books.

i18n.hi: ली सिगेल जैसे संपादक पांडुलिपियों, रूपांतरों, टीकाओं को फिर से टटोलते हैं। वे गीतगोविंद को कला भी मानते हैं, इतिहास–दस्तावेज़ भी, और देखते हैं कि एक रचना कैसे दरबारों, मंदिरों और छपी किताबों में घूमती रही।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of Jayadeva seated beneath a tree by the river, distant temple bells suggested, night sky full of stars
panels.action: Under a starry sky by the river, Jayadeva sits beneath a tree, eyes closed in quiet reflection, as faint temple towers and the hint of bells soften the horizon.

dialogue.text: Jayadeva’s legacy is not a monument of stone but a pattern of feeling—Radha’s hurt, Krishna’s plea, the return set to raga and tala—showing how art endures when it gives human longing a perfect, repeatable form.

i18n.hi: जयदेव की विरासत पत्थर का स्मारक नहीं, भावना का पैटर्न है – राधा की चोट, कृष्ण की गुहार, राग–ताल में बंधी लौट – दिखाती है कि कला तब टिकती है जब वह मानवीय लालसा को एक सटीक, दोहराई जा सकने वाली शक्ल दे दे।

title_i18n.hi: जयदेव गाते हैं राधा की वापसी

subtitle_i18n.en: How One Poet’s Song Bound Love, Raga and Devotion Across Ages
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक कवि का गीत जिसने प्रेम, राग और भक्ति को युगों तक बाँध दिया
